# Hyper Elements

> The content engine for agents: React components your agent writes, rendered to emails, pages, PDFs and images, checked in every client, with the fix for what's wrong.

Agents asked to preview or test an email in Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail, Yahoo Mail, AOL Mail or other email clients (a Hyper Elements design or any HTML email): follow the email-testing skill, https://www.hyperelements.dev/skills/email-testing.md (install: `npx skills add hyper-elements/hyper-elements --skill email-testing`). It previews the email in each client, shows each client's screenshot and lists what it changed. To write templates: the hyper-elements skill, https://www.hyperelements.dev/skills/hyper-elements.md.

Install: `npm i @hyper-elements/react`. Import elements from `@hyper-elements/react`. A design has one root (Email, Page, Document or Canvas); styles go in style={{ }}; space between blocks is the parent's gap (no margins); render() returns { html, text, diagnostics }; validate() checks without rendering; outline() prints the laid-out design as text. From the shell, with `npm i -D @hyper-elements/cli`: `npx hyper-elements check emails/ --json` validates each design (a module whose default export renders the root) and `npx hyper-elements render emails/` writes its output. See [Command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/cli).

To check an email or a page is easy to read (link words, alternate text, contrast, text size, headings, language, merge syntax typed by hand), use `@hyper-elements/lint`: `validate(email, { plugins: [lint()] })`, or `lintHtml(html)` from `@hyper-elements/lint/html` for any HTML email; the CLI runs it in `check`. See [Lint](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/lint).

To check existing HTML emails and preview Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail locally, use the JavaScript/TypeScript library `@hyper-elements/email-clients`: `npm i @hyper-elements/email-clients`, then `await renderInEmailClients(html)` takes the complete HTML string and returns previews and diagnostics. No React, account or test send is required. Each client, classic Outlook included, was reverse-engineered by testing thousands of emails in the real client, and the previews are 98% accurate on average, with classic Outlook drawn with Word's rules. From the shell, `npx @hyper-elements/cli check email.html` checks the email and `npx @hyper-elements/cli preview email.html` writes the preview files. The library also takes Hyper Elements Email templates. See [Email client emulator](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/email-client-emulator) for saving previews and the browser setup for CLI findings.
Open the [Email testing playground](https://www.hyperelements.dev/email-testing) to edit or paste complete HTML on the left and compare live email-client thumbnails on the right. Click a client to open its full preview, read compatibility diagnostics, and download them as a JSON report. Nothing is uploaded; referenced images and fonts may load from their hosts. Browser agents can call `window.hyperElementsEmailTesting.check({ html, dark: false })` (every client unless `clients` names some, such as `["outlook", "gmail", "apple-mail"]`), or use the WebMCP tool `check_html_email` where supported. Both return diagnostics, preview metadata (including approximate flags), and skipped variants. An `ok` result means generation succeeded, not that the email is guaranteed to render identically in real clients.
Open the [Open Graph image generator](https://www.hyperelements.dev/tools/open-graph-image-generator) to make a 1200 × 630 share image in the browser (six designs, a headline, a photo and a logo, PNG or JPG). Each design is a template (`@hyper-elements/react/template`) whose source the page shows, with a Next.js `opengraph-image` route and the CLI commands that draw one image per post with `renderImage()`.

## Get started

- [Introduction](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs): Hyper Elements is a set of React components that render one design to email-safe HTML, a web page, a PDF or an image.
- [Quickstart](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/quickstart): Install Hyper Elements, write a welcome email in JSX, render it to HTML and plain text, and send it with Resend.

## Core concepts

- [Designs](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/designs): A design is JSX with one root: Email, Page, Document or Canvas. The root decides the output. Root props, what goes inside, your own functions, and sharing content between roots.
- [Layout](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/layout): Arrange blocks with Section, Row, Column, Grid and Layer. Space with gap and padding, size with widths and flex shares, and stack on phones.
- [Styles](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/styles): Style elements with style={{ }} using CSS names. Phone styles go in its mobile block and hover styles in its hover block. Where phones start, hidden, fonts and text direction.
- [Rendering](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/rendering): render() turns a design into HTML and plain text, renderPdf() into a PDF and renderImage() into an image. Their results and options, validate() and outline(), merge tags, and where they run.
- [Themes](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/themes): Write a brand once with defineTheme() and give it to any root: tokens, roles the built-in elements read, each element's defaults and variants, named styles, and scopes that change tokens for one band.
- [Custom elements](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/custom-elements): Three ways to add something of your own: a plain function, defineElement() for a named block with typed and checked props, and Html for markup no element writes.
- [Command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/cli): Preview, check and render Hyper Elements designs from the shell with the hyper-elements command: a live page of your designs, the email client checks, and each design's HTML, PDF or image.

## Outputs

- [Email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/email): What the email writer produces from an Email root. Tables with px widths, Outlook's markup in conditional comments, phone styles, preview text and known limits.
- [Page](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/page): What a Page root renders to: semantic HTML and flexbox with inline styles, a small stylesheet for phones and hover, no client JavaScript, ready to embed.
- [PDF](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/pdf): Render a Document root to print-ready HTML, or to a PDF file with @hyper-elements/react/pdf on the server, with no browser and no network.
- [Image](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/image): Render a Canvas root to a PNG or SVG with @hyper-elements/react/image: social cards, Open Graph images and banners, on the server with no browser.

## Templates

- [Templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates): Reusable designs with guardrails: locked parts, typed fields, blocks and slots with their limits, and a check of the result before anything is rendered.
- [Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples): Four templates with their parts outlined, built step by step: a launch graphic in two sizes, an email with a locked header and footer around an open body, a newsletter with a limited body, and an invoice filled from data. Then the same from code.
- [Values: fields, images and formats](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields): The values a design gives a template: every kind of field, the rules an image field checks, formats, bindings, values as data and what describe() tells whoever fills a template.
- [Content: slots and blocks](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots): The content a design gives a template: slots (JSX someone writes, inside limits), blocks (approved section types, picked and ordered as data), and annotated templates.
- [Rules, checks and diagnostics](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules): The rules a template holds every design to, what its check() returns, the order it checks in, snapshots, the rules decided by measuring a Canvas, and every template diagnostic with what triggers it.
- [Templates in the command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli): Values files, design new and design set, TSX template designs, slots as modules, trusted templates, --require-template and template extract, with the hyper-elements CLI.

## Validation

- [Diagnostics](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/diagnostics): What validate() and render() report: ElementsError, severities, each diagnostic's code, message and path, the codes you'll meet, and checks in CI.
- [Test emails in Outlook and Gmail locally](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/email-client-emulator): Check existing HTML emails and preview Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail locally with a free JavaScript library or CLI. No React, account or test send required.
- [Lint](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/lint): @hyper-elements/lint checks an email or a page for what makes it hard to read: links that don't say where they go, images without alternate text, faint or small text, headings out of order, merge syntax typed by hand.

## Reference

- [Theme reference](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/themes/reference): Every part of defineTheme(): token rules, which tokens each style takes, element defaults by a prop's value, variants, named styles, the merge order, scopes, formats, extendTheme(), tokens in your own elements, typed names, and what each output writes.
- [Command line reference](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/cli/reference): Every hyper-elements command and its options: render's files, fonts and images, check and lint, preview's findings and browsers, HTML emails, dev, templates, the JSON output, exit codes, agents, and how the CLI runs designs.

## Guides

- [Sending email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/sending): Render a design once on your server, then hand its HTML and plain text to Resend, AWS SES, Postmark, SendGrid or Nodemailer.
- [Next.js](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/nextjs): Render emails in Next.js App Router route handlers and Server Components, with output that stays the same from one render to the next.
- [AI agents](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/ai-agents): Give your coding agent the Hyper Elements guide, and a loop to check its own designs, in code or from the shell: write, validate, outline, render, and check it in the email client emulator.
- [Agent benchmark](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/benchmark): Compare time to a passing email or image, output tokens and first-check passes across Hyper Elements and other approaches, using the same briefs and checks.
- [Visual editing](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/visual-editor): Turn a design into Unlayer design JSON for its builder with toDesign(), and read an edited builder design back as a design with fromDesign().

## Migrate

- [From React Email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/migrate/react-email): Move React Email templates to Hyper Elements with one command that converts each template and checks it against the original.
- [From Unlayer Elements](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/migrate/unlayer-elements): Move templates written with Unlayer Elements to Hyper Elements with a codemod that keeps your props, loops and helpers.

## Elements

- [Elements](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements): how every element takes its props and its style, and the full list
- [Values](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/values): What a property takes, where it says *kind*:
- [Email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/email): An email. Its children are stacked down the content width, centered in the window.
- [Page](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/page): A web page. Its children are stacked down the content width, centered in the window.
- [Document](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/document): A printed document: its children on pages of its size (Document.Page, or split by PageBreaks), a PageHeader and a PageFooter on each. Renders to print HTML, and to PDF with @hyper-elements/react/pdf.
- [Canvas](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/canvas): An image of a fixed size (a social card, a banner): its children laid out in it as on a page. Written as PNG or SVG with @hyper-elements/react/image.
- [Section](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/section): A band across the whole window, directly in an Email or Page: its background spans the window, its children are stacked at the content width.
- [Row](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/row): Lays its children out side by side. A child takes its width, or a share of what's left (its flex, 1 by default).
- [Column](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/column): Stacks its children vertically, with its own spacing and box.
- [Grid](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/grid): Its children in columns of equal width, row after row; on phones, one under another.
- [Layer](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/layer): Its children over each other, in one box as tall as the tallest: words on an image (a background image, its first child). In an email, an Image with one child over it.
- [Svg](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/svg): Shapes (Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Line, Polygon, Path) drawn in a box of its own: its width and height, and the coordinates its viewBox gives them.
- [Text](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/text): A paragraph of text.
- [Heading](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/heading): A heading, from level 1 (the page's title) to 6.
- [Button](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/button): A link drawn as a button.
- [Image](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/image): An image in the content. Without a width it takes its own size, no wider than its parent.
- [Divider](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/divider): A horizontal line.
- [List](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/list): A bulleted or numbered list of ListItems. Its markers sit in a column of their own (indent) before the items.
- [Table](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/table): A table of data: TableRows of TableCells. Columns take their cells' widths; the rest share what's left.
- [Video](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/video): A YouTube or Vimeo video: its player on a page; in an email (which can't play one), its thumbnail, linked to it.
- [Social](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/social): Links to social profiles: a line of the networks' icons, each linked to its profile.
- [Menu](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/menu): A line of links (a site's sections, a footer's), onto more lines where they don't fit, with a separator between them on desktop; or links down a column.
- [Html](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/html): Markup written as it is, for what no element says (the builder's HTML block): in an email and on a page as given, nothing in it checked or escaped. A Document's PDF and a Canvas's image draw its plain text.
- [PageNumber](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagenumber): In a Document's text: the number of the page it's on, or (total) how many pages there are.
- [Span](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/span): Styled text inside text; raised or lowered (superscript, subscript) with verticalAlign.
- [Link](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/link): A link: text inside text, or around an Image.
- [LineBreak](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/linebreak): Starts a new line inside text.
- [MergeTag](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/mergetag): A value the sending service fills in (a name, a link), written in the service's own syntax.
- [Document.Page](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/document-page): One page of a Document (Document.Page in JSX): its children stacked down it, inside the Document's margins.
- [PageBreak](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagebreak): In a Document, where a page ends: what follows starts the next page.
- [PageHeader](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pageheader): In a Document: drawn at the top of every page, inside its margins.
- [PageFooter](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagefooter): In a Document: drawn at the bottom of every page, inside its margins.
- [ListItem](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/listitem): An item of a List: text, and a List of its own to nest one.
- [TableRow](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/tablerow): A row of a Table. A header row's cells are header cells, in bold.
- [TableCell](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/tablecell): A cell of a TableRow: text, and images. Its width sets its column's.
- [Rect](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/rect): A rectangle at x, y in its Svg, rounded by rx.
- [Circle](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/circle): A circle centered at cx, cy in its Svg.
- [Ellipse](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/ellipse): An ellipse centered at cx, cy in its Svg.
- [Line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/line): A straight line from x1, y1 to x2, y2 in its Svg (drawn by its stroke).
- [Polygon](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/polygon): A closed shape through its points ("0,0 40,0 20,30"), in its Svg.
- [Path](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/path): A shape drawn by an SVG path (d), in its Svg.

## Templates

- [Templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates): ready-made emails, pages, PDFs and images as plain Elements JSX, each drawn in a brand; copy one and its brand.ts
- [Review received](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/airbnb-review): Email. A guest's review, shown to the host once the review period ends: the logo, the reviewer's photo, their words in a shaded box, a button to reply, and common questions
- [App Store receipt](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/apple-receipt): Email. A subscription's receipt: the order's details in a gray table, the app with its icon and price, the total, an offer, and the fine print
- [Event invitation](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/event): Email. An invitation: the event's name on a band of the brand's color, when and where, a button to register, and the day's schedule
- [Invoice email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/invoice): Email. The email that sends an invoice: the amount due, the due date, the lines, and a button to pay online
- [Magic link](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/magic-link): Email. A one-time link that signs the reader in, how long it works, and a note for when they didn't ask
- [Newsletter](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/newsletter): Email. A regular issue: a locked masthead and footer, with the issue, an unsubscribe link and the company's address, around a body of sections the issue writes
- [It's on its way](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/nike-shipping): Email. An order that has shipped: the tracking number and a button up top, a bold headline, where it's going, the item with its picture, picks for you, and help
- [Order confirmation](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/order-confirmation): Email. An order confirmed: its number and date, the items with the total, and where it's going
- [Password reset](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/password-reset): Email. A link to choose a new password, how long it works, and what to do if the reader didn't ask
- [Receipt](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/receipt): Email. A payment receipt that leads with the amount paid, then the items, the total, and how it was paid
- [Shipping](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/shipping): Email. An order on its way: when it should arrive, who's carrying it, a button to track it, and what's in the box
- [Sign-in code](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/sign-in-code): Email. A one-time code, large and centered in a box of its own, with when it expires and what to do if it wasn't you
- [Welcome to Premium](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/spotify-premium): Email. A paid plan that has just started: a big headline, what it gives you, one pill button, the plan and its price, and the apps
- [Stack Overflow tips](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/stack-overflow-tips): Email. A tips issue: the logo on the page, a banner with the headline beside its art, ruled sections with a list of tips, one button, and a footer with the email's settings and the address
- [Stripe welcome](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/stripe-welcome): Email. The email once an account can take live payments: the logo, short paragraphs with links into the docs, one button, and the address
- [Verify email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/verify-email): Email. One step before the account is ready: confirm the email address it was made with
- [Welcome](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/emails/welcome): Email. A greeting on a band of the brand's color, three numbered next steps, and one button
- [Event page](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/pages/event): Web page. An event's web page: its name and tagline on a band of the brand's color, when and where, the schedule, and the speakers
- [Trip receipt](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/airbnb-receipt): PDF. A stay's receipt as a PDF: the logo and receipt ID, where and when, the guests, the price night by night with fees and taxes, how it was paid, and the cancellation policy
- [Certificate](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/certificate): PDF. A certificate on a landscape page: a double frame, the recipient's photo and name, what they achieved, the date, a seal, and the signer's signature
- [Invoice](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/invoice): PDF. An invoice as a PDF: the letterhead, who it's billed to, the lines with their sums, the total due, and page numbers
- [Quote](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/quote): PDF. A quote as a PDF: who it's for, the work with its prices, the estimated total, how long it holds, and lines to sign it
- [Receipt](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/receipt): PDF. A receipt as a PDF: paid in full, with the items, the total, the date and how it was paid
- [Stripe invoice](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/stripe-invoice): PDF. An invoice as Stripe's PDFs lay it out: the title and logo, its numbers and dates, from and bill to, the amount due with a link to pay, the lines, the totals, and a footer on every page
- [Ticket](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/documents/ticket): PDF. A ticket as a PDF: the event on a band of the brand's color, who it's for, when and where, and the code to show at the door
- [Launch graphic](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/images/announcement): Image. A product launch for social posts: a line above a headline fitted to three lines, up to four features, and the product shown in a window over artwork
- [Product drop post](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/images/nike-drop): Image. A new product for a social feed, 1080 by 1080: a huge headline in capitals, what it is and when, and the product's photo on a pale panel
- [Open Graph card](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/images/og-card): Image. A link preview, 1200 by 630: the title fitted to three lines, the brand's logo and site, and shapes in its colors
- [Speaker card](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/images/speaker): Image. A card announcing one speaker, for social posts: their photo in a circle over shapes in the brand's colors, their name and role, their talk in a block of color, and the event and date
- [Wrapped share card](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates/images/spotify-wrapped): Image. A year in listening as a story to share, 1080 by 1920: bold shapes, the minutes listened, the top artists and songs, and the top genre

## Developer tutorials

- [Automate Open Graph images for every page in Next.js](https://www.hyperelements.dev/blog/automate-open-graph-images-nextjs): Give every Next.js page an on-brand Open Graph image made from its title, drawn at build time from one template, with a build that fails on a title that doesn't fit.
- [Check HTML emails in GitHub Actions without rewriting your templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/blog/html-email-checks-github-actions): Check existing HTML emails in GitHub Actions with Hyper Elements, fail on warnings, and keep machine-readable diagnostics without changing template frameworks.
- [Generate Open Graph images in Node.js with local fonts and a logo](https://www.hyperelements.dev/blog/node-open-graph-images-local-fonts): Generate branded Open Graph PNGs from React in Node.js using local fonts and a logo, with a reusable template, diagnostics and long-title checks.
- [Generate PDF invoices in Node.js without headless Chrome](https://www.hyperelements.dev/blog/node-pdf-invoices-without-chrome): Build a React invoice PDF in Node.js with local fonts, a logo, explicit pages and useful diagnostics. Includes a complete template and current limitations.
- [Build and validate React emails with Claude Code](https://www.hyperelements.dev/blog/react-emails-claude-code): Build a receipt email with Claude Code, fix template diagnostics, inspect its layout and render HTML and plain text for a test send.
